title: My stack, my experience, building a procedurally drawn yet 'pixel feeling' game. AMA!
author: sseses
selftext:
My experience so far has been that chatgpt is a good model for understanding how a game looks and feels, claude is not so good at that...

The thing that is working for me is to to have gpt or claude write tools for itself that help it obey rules around anatomy, body mechanics and visual feel. thats how i keep it consistent. I'm doing a lot of procedural drawing as well. So much so that it broke the performance of my game with Godot 4.6.x and I wrote a custom rust plugin in order to bake the frames much faster and with less memory penalty. The nice thing about procedural drawing though is that once you have a system, its really easy to apply overarching changes on reused components and in general maintain a really consistent feel to your overall art.

My stack:  
\* Claude Code, ChatGPT Codex,  and AGY (astra in particular has been really great, but eats credits much faster). 

\* AGY and codex are my main 'visual critics' and claude my heavyhitter project manager & technical coder.  
\* Rust godot modules to optimize taxing parts of game  
\* Suno for some music, but alot is synths tuned by ear + chatgpt composing.  
  
I have been a developer for 20 years, and using ai to code has been a wild ride for roughly the last year or so for me. Excitement, adjusting, and ultimately learning to love these tools.  
  
Heres the game I've been building with my compadre for the last 2 months. A slightly old demo is available. No ads or spam -- just pure indie energy here. I'd love feedback.

comments.body: how much help is AI on procedually generated content? 2d and 3d low poly

replies.author: sseses
replies.body:
I started with some hand drawn and some pixel lab images. All the bipedal art and most of the scene art like buildings is all procedural now. AI Its a ton of help. So far the best model for building procedural art and animations for me has been Astra.Tthere is a tuning though of style how you want your art to look so i think thats where having a starting point or concept art at the beginning helps.

Once I had concept art and some basic requirements it was easy for Astra to animate everything I needed procedurally (but I had it loop back on looking at renderings of its own procedural art so it got better and better at it -- and I'd have it put its learnings back into agent skill files regularly).
